strings.name: Adele
strings.summary: Raised in London, Adele entered recording after training at a performing arts school. Her forceful, nuanced singing connects soul traditions with personal accounts of relationships, loss and growing older. The albums 19, 21, 25 and 30 mark different stages of her life and reached audiences through recordings and live performance. Her awards include multiple Grammys and an original-song Oscar shared with Paul Epworth for “Skyfall.”
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. The selected chronology extends to the November 2025 casting announcement; a planned film is not presented as released. Albums and performances are selected milestones, not a complete news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Influenced global pop through albums including 21 and 25 and distinctive vocal expression, sustaining traditions of soul music and personal storytelling.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Graduated from the BRIT School in 2006
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Voice and personal narrative
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Albums including 21 and 25 brought soul influences, expressive singing and intimate emotional experience to a broad pop audience.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Writing for cinema
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Co-wrote “Skyfall” with Paul Epworth; the song won the 2013 Academy Award for original song.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Cast in Cry to Heaven
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Reports announced her casting in Tom Ford’s adaptation of Anne Rice’s novel; the announcement does not establish a completed release.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Concludes her Las Vegas residency
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Gave the final Weekends with Adele performance, closing a residency that had run for two years.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Begins Weekends with Adele
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Opened a residency at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas, presenting songs from her catalogue in a theatre setting.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Releases 30
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Released an album exploring divorce, motherhood and self-understanding, continuing her age-based album titles.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: 25 and “Hello” win Grammys
strings.timeline.event-05.text: 25 won Album of the Year, while “Hello” won Record and Song of the Year, among other awards.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Releases 25
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Led by “Hello,” the album revisited growing older and the passage of time, extending her international recording career.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: “Skyfall” wins an Oscar
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Shared the original-song award with Paul Epworth for the theme to the James Bond film of the same name.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Wins six Grammys in one ceremony
strings.timeline.event-08.text: 21 and recordings including “Rolling in the Deep” earned six awards, including Album, Record and Song of the Year.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Releases 21
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Songs including “Rolling in the Deep” and “Someone Like You” combined soul influences and breakup narratives, expanding her audience.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Releases her debut album 19
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Released her debut, including “Chasing Pavements,” and won the Grammy for Best New Artist the following year.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Graduates and signs with XL
strings.timeline.event-11.text: After graduating from the BRIT School, circulating demo recordings helped her secure a deal with XL Recordings.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Born in London
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Born in Tottenham, London; she grew up listening to pop and soul and later pursued performing arts education.
